articleTitle: A Novel Automatic Ghost Canceller
abstract: Ghost is one of the most serious problems in TV reception. Ghost reduction is highly desirable, and some automatic deghosting systems have been reported [1] ,[2] [3], [4]. All the systems utilize transversal filters. The approach with a transversal filter may be the best way.

articleTitle: A High Performance Color CRT Gun with an Asymmetrical Beam Forming Region
abstract: In recent years there has been a growing international trend toward the display of teletext type information on a color TV screen'. This trend requires improvement in the corner readability of the in-line CRT.

articleTitle: A Description of the Broadcast Telidon System
abstract: Telidon, the Canadian videotex standard, is now a familiar concept, and its operation in the interactive mode via the switched telephone network has been well documented. This paper presents the transmission format used for Telidon data carried as an ancillary signal on broadcast television channels. We shall first review some of the essential characteristics of Telidon, and then show that these are preserved in the broadcast situation.

articleTitle: A Unifying Principle Behind Switching Converters and some New Basic Configurations
abstract: Switching converters are conventionally drawn in three basic configurations, namely, a) The Flyback converter b) The Forward Converter c) The Up-Converter Each of these configurations is characterised by a D. C. voltage transfer of the form where Vo and V1 are respectively, the output and input voltages, and d is the duty-ratio of the switch. To the extent that F(d) is different for each of the three configurations, they are considered to differ from each other in a basic, mathematical, sense.

articleTitle: Novel IC Structure for 150V High-Voltage Consumer IC
abstract: This paper describes a novel IC structure and its fabrication process for 150V high voltage consumer ICs. A color TV vertical deflection output IC which operates with a transformerless voltage source has been developed.

articleTitle: A New Approach to a High Performance Electron Gun Design for Color Picture Tubes
abstract: At present a narrow neck (29 mm) in-line color picture tube in combination with a self-convergent deflection yoke is the most widely used TV-display system. This popularity comes from its easy convergence adjustment, low cost and power saving. However, the disadvantage of the system is its limited resolution, because the main lens of the electron gun has been narrowed to about half that of the wide neck delta system. The astigmatic deflection field also deterio- rates resolution at the edge of the picture.

articleTitle: Monolithic Integrated VHF TV Tuner
abstract: Using an NSA (Nitride Self-Aligned) bipolar process with 4 GHz fT transistors, a monolithic frequency converter IC was developed, which consisted of a local oscillator, mixer, IF amplifier, UHF-IF amplifier, AGC amplifier and voltage regulator.

articleTitle: High Quality Parcor Speech Synthesizer
abstract: A high quality speech synthesizer system which consists of 3 LSI chips, a speech synthesizer, a 128k bit ROM and a general purpose microprocessor has been developed. This system is based on the recently developed Partial Autocorrelation (PARCOR) voice compression technique. This system can generate high quality speech from a data rate of less than 2400 bits per second. Several new techniques are applied for this system to improve the quality of generated speech especially of the female voice. This system has many advantageous features such as speech speed control and external pitch excitation.

articleTitle: A Piezo Powered IC Transmitter
High Performance UHF Varactor Tuner with a Dual-Gate GaAs Mesfet and GaAs Varactor Diodes
abstract: It has become necessary to improve the performance of UHF varactor tuners with the recent popularization of UHF TV broadcasting. Their performance is generally poor in noise figure, cross modulation and image signal immunity.

articleTitle: CCD Digital Color Camera
abstract: An experimental color camera using a green CC: D(charge-coupled device) and a red and blue CCD and employing digital signal processing has been developed. The highly-stable camera is capable of excellent color reproduction with no adjustment. Digital processing is particularly appropriate because CCD imagers are essentially two-dimensional spatial sampling systems. Another advantage of digital processing is that, with recent progress in digital circuitry, it is now possible for a great number of the camera's logic functions to be realized in a few LSIs.

articleTitle: Electronic Reduction of FM Distortion Caused by Multipath Transmission
abstract: Multipath transmission of FM radio waves produces a considerable amount of distortion which is the main cause of sound deterioration in FM broadcasting reception, and this problem is especially severe in the urban or mountainous regions.

articleTitle: A Base-Band Comb Filter for Consumer Television Receivers
abstract: Since the inception of color TV twenty-five years ago, there has been a continual improvement in the performance and features available in consumer television receivers. Advancements in circuit and device technologies have made their way from the research laboratories into consumer products as economics has permitted. So it is that now the circuit techniques of comb filtering, which have been known for decades, have become viable in consumer TV through the recent advancements in charge coupled devices and in MOS integrated circuits. These technologies can now be married with TV circuit designs to open new realms of picture resolution, freedom from interference between the luminance and chrominance signals and a new dimension of picture sharpness through the addition of vertical detail enhancement.

articleTitle: A Sound Field Effector for Car Stereo
abstract: Car stereo sets have been increasingly used in passenger cars. However, in passenger cars there are several disadvantages for sound reproduction compared with listening rooms, that is, the acoustical effects such as the reverberant sound effects and the sound expanding effects are inadequate for the reasons that cabins are very narrow, and the left and right loudspeakers are usually arranged asymmetrically to the listeners and installed in restricted spaces. Therefore, it is difficult to reproduce live stereo sound in passenger cars.

articleTitle: TV Tuners Using Low Loss and Low Distortion GaAs Varactor Diodes
abstract: The noise figure of conventional TV varactor tuners is fairly high, when typical Si diodes, whose average resistance is 0.65Ω at 470 MHz, are used. Low noise tuners which comply with FCC noise requirements can be realized if low loss varactor diodes are developed. However, Si diodes with still lower losses can not be manufactured by conventional Si process technology with high production yield. Low noise Si rf transistors with a noise figure of 1.3 dB at 470 MHz is commercially available. However, noise figure improvement using these transistors at 470 MHz is only 1.0 ~ 1.2 dB when compared with conventional tuners. These low noise Si transistors are high in cost and low in production yield because the specification uniformities are insufficient.

articleTitle: The First Electronic Speech Circuit Opens the Way to the Fully-Electronic Telephone
abstract: This paper shows how the speech circuit in a conventional carbon microphone may be replaced by a new monolithic integrated circuit, leading to the implementation of a fully electronic set.

articleTitle: A Single-ECL/12L-Chip PLL IC for Frequency Synthesized TV Tuning System
abstract: A microcomputer-controlled PLL bipolar IC including prescalers,has been developed. The ECL circuit contains a wideband band buffer amplifier and a high speed (1.2 GHz) prescaler. The I2L circuit contains all the PLL logic functions. A novel digitally-controlled frequency offset circuit using a 3 modulo prescaler and a rate multiplier, was designed in order to detune the local oscillator frequency from the center in the ±2MHz (±1 MHz) range with 31.25KHz(15.625KHz) steps. It makes this IC applicable to any nation's TV channel frequency. A new IC technology realizes both a high fT (4GHz) linear transistor and a high speed I2L gate (tpd=7n sec for a single collector) on the same chip.

articleTitle: A New Voltage Regulator Protects the Automotive Electronics
abstract: As electronics begins to play an ever increasing rôle of importance in automotive electronics, so the demand for higher reliability becomes ever more evident. This reliability must be assured under conditions which, for electronic devices, are severe to say the least.

articleTitle: Television Design Aspects foe Better Teletext Reception
abstract: In our attempt to adapt the Teletext service to the United States, we should first consider the differences between the basic broadcast system of the United States and that of other countries.

articleTitle: New Chrominance Signal Processing LSI for Home VCR
abstract: The home VCR is the most complicated home electronic appliance and employs an extremely large number of electronic components. Therefore, with the home VCR, it is difficult to ensure high reliability and consistent performance. This difficulty, however, can be overcome in the most effective way by reducing the number of components employed in the VCR (especially that of active parts) through extensive use of ICs in its circuitry.

articleTitle: VCR Signal Dropout Counter
abstract: Recently compact video tape recorders for home use have become popular throughout the world and their performance and picture quality are generally satisfactory. One of the biggest problems tending to degrade the playback picture is the dropout phenomenon.

articleTitle: Integrated SHF Converter Formed on a Single Teflon-Fiberglas Substrate
abstract: We have successfully developed a high performance SHF TV converter which converts 12 GHz incoming signal down to UHF TV band.

articleTitle: Frequency Synthesizing Tuning System with Saw Device
abstract: Recently many kinds of TV digital tuning systems have been developed. Especially in the United States the PLL frequency synthesizing method has been widely used. This system has advantages such as 10-key direct addressing, digital channel indication, high stability and accuracy of the local oscillator frequency, and so on. However it has also disadvantages such as harmonic interferences caused by a 1000 MHz ECL prescaler, and radiation from the prescaler which needs a large input level of 0.3 ~ 1 Vp-p.

articleTitle: A Novel Arc-Suppression Technique for Cathode Ray Tubes
abstract: As an increasing number of ICs are expected to be used in the circuits of future TV receivers, it is very important to devise a simple and effective method of protecting essential electrical components from destructive high. voltage arcing.

articleTitle: A High Speed NMOS PLL-Synthesizer LSI with on-Chip Prescaler for AM/FM Receivers
abstract: Although more than twenty years have passed by since the advent of IC technology, our most concern to the IC technology has been focussed to direct yet one-sided quantities such as device packing density and operational speed. Even today, in our LSI's most prosperous age, the memory capacity and the speed- power product of the ring oscillators are most treasured as the expression of the height of the technological level. 2 These facts seem refering to us that our conventional IC concept has not been freed from 'cluster of discrete devices'.

articleTitle: Two-CCD Color Television Camera
abstract: A new solid-state color television camera has been developed using charge-coupled devices (CCD) which have 174,080 (512V X340H) picture elements. High resolution and fine color fidelity pictures practicable for commercial use are obtained using two CCDS and a yellow-white color stripe filter.

articleTitle: The Promise of Teletext for Hearing-Impaired Audiences
Microprocessor Controlled Variable Play-Back Speed System for Video Tape Recorder
abstract: A new home use video tape recorder with features of varying play-back speed is required for further attractive application of VTR especially in the field of sports, such as in training and form correction.

articleTitle: A New High-Resolution Trinitron Color Picture Tube for Display Application
abstract: Recent progress in high-speed electronic computers capable of processing a great number of input data calls for the development of a high-resolution color display device. Among the proposed display devices, the cathode ray tube continues to offer many advantages and promises to be the dominant device for the foreseeable future. The resolution and picture quality of the cathode ray system, however, must be improved for this new application.

articleTitle: Data Analysis Procedures and Presentation Formats for Broadcast Teletext Field Tests
abstract: In conjunction with the activities of the Electronic Industries Association (EIA): Efforts to develop a U.S. recommended standard for Broadcast Teletext, the author describes the objectives of field tests being conducted under EIA auspices. Test hardware and methods which permit real time capture of data are identified and discussed. The need for performing testing which is independent of a specific hardware or system implementation is set forth. Data analysis methods and procedures which reduce the raw captured data to a form which can be used to realize the objectives of the testing are described. Samples of presentation formats developed by the author are exhibited. These sample presentation formats are analyzed to demonstrate how they might be used for actual data, to derive insights into performance of a Teletext system at various data transmission rates.

articleTitle: Playcable: a Technological Alternative for Information Services
The Application of Picture Coding Techniques to Viewdata
abstract: In March 1980 the British Post Office described research that has led to a facility for inserting high quality coloured pictures in viewdata pages. The technique is to use picture coding technology (originally devised for surveillanrce and teleconferencing) to reduce the number of bits required so that the use of low bandwidth circuits is feasible. This paper gives further technical details and describes some possible applications. A brief account of the current state of viewdata activities in the UK is included to explain why this development is regarded as important.

articleTitle: FM Multipath Distortion in Automobile Receivers has been Significantly Reduced by a New Antenna System
abstract: Multipath interference is one of the most serious problems for mobile receivers. To reduce interference many methods and systems have been developed. Two most effective methods are space diversity and electrical cancellation of the interference. The latter method needs not only some complex circuitry such as microprocessor but also a relatively long adjusting time. On the other hand space diversity has comparatively simple electrical structure and is easily realized by means of adequate antennas and their control circuits. The problem of space diversity especially for automobile reception is that a large space is required for a good diversity effect. Therefore, these two methods are not suitable for mobile FM receivers.

articleTitle: Dynamically Redefinable Character SETS-D.R.C.S.
abstract: D. R. C. S. is potentially the most powerful and cost effective editorial addition to the Teletext and Viewdata services of all the refinements that have been discussed and proposed at various committees on these new public services.

articleTitle: PLL IC Capable of Direct Division of FM Local Oscillator Frequency
abstract: Recently, a PLL frequency synthesizer, one of the applications of a phase-locked loop ( PLL ), has become popular with the advancement of IC technologies. It is, however, considerably difficult to apply it to high frequency systems such as FM radio tuners. 1)

articleTitle: Low Cost 8-Bit Songle Chip Microcomputer Simplifies Softward and I/O Control in Consumer Applications
abstract: The phenomenal growth of single chip microcomputers in consumer products has generated greater demand for devices with increased performance capabilities. Microcomputer manufacturers have responded to the demand for increased performance by introducing devices with greater system integration. As a result, functions previously incorporated in several discrete packages have been brought "on chip" reducing package count, board real estate usage, and cost.

articleTitle: A New Monochrome Data/Graphics Video Projector
abstract: This paper gives an outline of the user requirements for and the design principles involved in a new compact monochrome video projector. The unit is specifically intended for high resolution large screen display of alphanumeric and graphic information of computer generated signals. Emphasis has been placed on the ease of customer set up and the projector's overall versatility. A high brightness output allcws use on flat or rear projection screens that may already be in place. To obtain a better contrast ratio in higher ambient light enviroments, a higher gain curved screen is normally used to reject unwanted light. This large display medium provides an excellent man/machine interface for large groups of people involved in all kinds of computer software and hardware demonstrations. It also readily displays "on line" information for sales clinics, business boardrooms, stock and comnodity exchanges and airports. A trip to any recent computer trade show finds several exhibitors trying to display their wares on bulky, low performance consumer projection television sets which were designed for different requirements. To match these needs, the new design employs a unique combination of lens, CRT, and electronics expertise in a small, lightweight and economical package.

articleTitle: A Quality Scalling Easure for Integrated Communications
abstract: Since the inception of color television twenty-five years ago, there has been a continual development of technology in the areas of electro-optic devices, materials for recording electrical signcils, and integrated electronic subsysteins. Advancements in these areas have made their way from the research laboratory into ancillary products surrounding the modern day television set. The color television screen is rapidly becoming the primary tool for machines to display information to man for entertainment, training, business, or personal reasons.

articleTitle: The Impact of Semi-Custom IC'S on Automative Applications
abstract: The availability of semi-custom component and gate arrays has improved significantly in the last few years. Many different technologies have been put to use, particularly in the field of Gate Arrays. This, in turn, has stimulated the use of semi-custom IC's in the marketplace, and the automotive market has been no exception.

articleTitle: Designing Tracking Error-Free Varactor Tuners with Frequency Locked Loop Integrated Circuits
A 1 GHz Low Power 2 Modulus Frequency Divider
abstract: This paper presents a high speed frequency divider which performs 2-modulus operation with the division ratio of 128 and 136 at a. frequency range over 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Creeping Discharge in Color Picture Tubes
abstract: Glow due to stray emission, dark current, interelectrode arcing, arcing, and leakage current among electrodes, is a measure to exhibit the high voltage stability of picture tubes. Especially since arcing may seriously damage integrated circuits (ICs), solid state devices and components in the circuitry or the picture tube itself, consequently the discharge-protection circuitry is applied to the chassis, and the picture tube is processed in various ways to prevent foreign substances and stray emission sources, which may cause the arcing, from being assembled inside the tube in the manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Resistance of GaAS Varactor Diodes for TV Tuners
abstract: Gallium arsenide varactor diodes have been extensively used in microwave applications because of high Q. But few papers have reported the diodes for UHF use, 1,2) although strongly requested to realize low noise TV tuners satisfying with the FCC noise figure requirement. In order to cover wide tuning frequency range as is used in TV UHF broadcasting band with varactor diodes, hyperabrupt diodes are needed. Hyper-abrupt GaAs diodes have been manufactured by a double epitaxial growth technique.1,2) These diodes for microwave use are commercially available.

articleTitle: Microprocessor Control for Color-TV Receivers
abstract: A microprocessor control that makes available sophisticated and desirable features not feasible with current standard or custom IC's is described. The TV controller features modular design, which permits essential functions to be implemented on a priority basis while events of secondary importance are held until processing time is available. Physical modularity also permits features to be added in the form of software changes, thus saving manufacturers the expense in time and money of hardware redesign.

articleTitle: Comparative Terminal Realizations with Alpha-Geometric Coding
abstract: The introduction of videotex services in several countries has spurred the search for the lowest cost user terminal which will provide acceptable performance. This has led to many arguments on the quality of graphics required. One faction argues that videotex is basically an alpha-numeric information service and only limited block graphics are required to enhance the text. The other faction argues that good graphics are an essential part of a videotex information service and are required to effectively communicate the information. Because of the wide range of information to be provided by videotex services it is likely that both faCtions are correct and in fact a wide range of terminals will be required. In the opinion of the authors of this paper, the graphics coding scheme used for videotex services should be capable of accommodating these variable terminal requirements and permit a maximum cf independence between the terminal, the communications medium used, and the data bases. In other words, a single data base should be capable of serving terminals with a variety of graphics qualities over a variety of communications mediums without any need for special processing for any particular terminal.

articleTitle: One Chip AM/FM Digital Tuning System
abstract: AM/FM radio receivers with a digital tuning system are increasing in number, spreading from car radios to home stereos. A phase locked loop (PLL) frequency synthesized tuning system is the best answer for the reccent demands, that is, tuning accuracy, stability, easiness of operation and easiness of function expansion.

articleTitle: A Temperature Stabilized Tachometer for the Fuel Efficient Automobile
abstract: In this day of energy conversion and high petroleum costs the optimum consumption of fuel is the goal of all owners of gas and diesel vehicles. The tachometer used with internal combustion engines permits engine revolution monitoring and with proper driver control increased kilometers per litre. The use of electronic automobile tachometers has not been popular because their linearity throughout the necessary RPM range leaves much to be desired due to their temperature instability. This report gives details of the design of a temperature-stable diode-pump automobile tachometer. The use of an unbalanced bridge circuit to interface the diode pump was found to reduce the changes in pump count caused by a temperature gradient. The original work, as reported here, was designed for a hand held instrument to be used by a mechanic. The identical circuitry has been applied to a digital-readout dashboard-mounted automobile tachometer. Diesel engines have used an inductance pick-up from the timing mark groove on the flywheel.

articleTitle: A Portable All-Band Radio Receiver Using Microcomputer Controlled PLL Synthesizer
abstract: With the recent advance of digital technology, we have been seeing a rapid inroad of frequency counters and PLL synthesizers even into radio receivers(1) and stereo tuners.

articleTitle: A New Tuning System With Non-Volatile Analog Memory
abstract: Electronic tuning systems are roughly classified into two categories. One is a frequency synthesizer system and the other is a voltage synthesizer system. The system described in this paper is the latter one.

articleTitle: A New Signal, Sync, and Scan Processor
abstract: Presented in this paper is a monolithic integrated circuit intended to provide high performance by careful selection of circuit techniques, and efficient partitioning of the AGC, sync. separatorr and master scan phase-locked loop.

articleTitle: Ladder Network Calculations
abstract: A program is described that will analyze most ladder networks considered for communications systems. With each branch consisting of four elements, the input impedance, transfer impedance, voltage transfer ratio, insertion loss, and group delay for five branches can be analyzed with a TI-58 calculator.

articleTitle: The Computer that will be in your Car
abstract: Need is indeed, the mother of invention. For decades, in this country, a prime critera of the automobile manufacturers' was large comfortable "muscle" cars. This is what the public wanted and the automotive market was (and still is) a buyers' market. Small gas efficient foreign cars were a rarity until the 1970s. (It should be noted that gasoline in most foreign countries has been relatively very expensive for 20-30 years.) Why did the American public demand the large cars? Several reasons-American gas was among the cheapest in the world, the cars were lightly taxed, they were affortable for most middle class budgets, and a large shiny car was a prestigious status symbol that "one had arrived" at prosperity.

articleTitle: Tiered Services Delivery and Control
abstract: The means to deliver, control and protect tiered services will be discussed in this paper. As the premium TV component of cable programming continues to grow, it will increase in value. The entertainment fare of today will be supplemented by other cable services. All of these services must be not only protected from theft, but also be directed to specific subscribers. This paper surveys the delivery and control systems commonly used in cable systems today. The paper moves from the simple protective schemes of the past through more stringent security, into addressability. These items are surveyed from the marketing point of view. It is the intent of this paper to indicate those characteristics of cable system control and delivery which provide opportunities for future engineering development.

articleTitle: The μP: The Key to An Advanced Frequency Synthesized HF SSB Amateur Radio Transceiver
abstract: Today's customer demands for more value (as measured by performance, operating ease, cost, etc.) are being met, in part, by the inicreasing use of microprocessors (μP). Frequently the, μP not only proves to be essential to the achievemeent of product design objectives from a marketing standpoint but also gives the engineeit seeveral advantages such as 1) an enhanced ability to deal with "change" Change in product definition or changes caused by design errors/oversights found during the development cycle. 2) a more cost effective design-frequently with fewer parts. 3) fewer design constraints between submodules due to the integrating capability of the μP.

articleTitle: Antiope Teletext Captioning
abstract: There is no need to argue the case for captioning, insofar as TV programs are already being captioned using tried and proven technology. However, it is a well-known fact that there is a demand for much more than classic captioning systems can provide. It would therefore seem that the time has come to extend captioning possibilities through the use of new techniques.

articleTitle: Distributorless Electronic Advance Ignition
abstract: An ignition system, is described which performs the functions of speed and vacuum advance, dwell control, current regulation, and stall shutdown with a single custom integrated circuit. Position sensing is from the flywheel, eliminating the need for a distributor.

articleTitle: Efficient Small-Size Antenna for FM Radio Reception
abstract: Functions required for the FM radio receiving system including antenna are mainly interference rejection and sensitivity, and are now demanded to be more improved in the face of an increase of FM broadcasting stations.

articleTitle: Microcontrollers-"System-Designed" Single-Chip Microcomputers Cut Manufacturing Costs
Antiope and D. R. C. S.
abstract: This paper describes a new technique called D. R. C. S. which is extremely helpful in text oriented communication systems: it provides through a very low cost user's terminal nearly unlimited repertoire of characters to be displayed for alphabetic applications and also fine graphics where they are needed. The integration of the feature to the French Antiope (1) Teletext or Teletel Videotex services is then discussed.

articleTitle: AM-FM Car Radio for Tomorrow
abstract: A new AM-FM monolithic integrated circuit for application in car radio is described with a particular emphasis on those points that are very critical for such an application.

articleTitle: Teletext Receiver a Circuit Design of the Sampling Clock Regeneration
abstract: In recent years Television multiplex broadcasting systems have been put into practical use or have been under investigations in different parts of the world. The development of one kind of Teletext receiver with the means of generating a hard copy began in early 1969 at Matsushita Electric Industrial Co., Ltd. (MEI).(1) In mid 1971, we started to examine a kind of receiver which could receive both Teletext signals and the Data sent on telephone lines.(2) MEI developed the original system of Japanese Teletext under the guidance of the Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK). We also developed the receiver and the test signal generator of UK Teletext in the middle of 1977.(3) The main body of this paper considers the method of the sampling clock regeneration of the Teletext receiver. We studied mainly the Japanese Teletext system which is now under consideration by the Radio Wave Technical Council, but most of the results can be applied to UK Teletext and others like it.

articleTitle: Color Signal Processing with New Band Width Compression Technique for a VCR
abstract: Chrominance signal processing, for Home VCR including slanted azimuth recording types such as VHS1) or Beta2), is based on heterodyning down the color information. This method is called the Color Under method3). It is superior to other methods in its small occupied band width and low moire level, but it has the following disadvantages.

articleTitle: Movies that Talk Back
abstract: TV movies that respond to words spoken by viewers can simulate entertaining face-to-face conversations between each viewer and screen actors or cartoon characters in the movie. The actors and cartoons will reply responsively with lip-sync sound to words spoken by viewers. Different audio and video frames can be addressed on a videodisc to provide one of several alternative replies or alternative actions at each branch point in the movie, depending on what the viewer says to a speech-recognition unit. A simple speech-recognition unit can be used because the number of words to be recognized at each branch point is restricted to just a few words. Different words are used at different branch points to make the dialog realistic. To inform viewers of what words they can use at each branch point, a menu of prompting words is displayed on a hand-held unit. These prompting words are programmed to be phonetically distinct to be easily distinguishable from each other. A viewer speaks one of the displayed words and the speech-recognition unit decides which of the expected words was spoken. Viewers can input questions or make other remarks by speaking a displayed code word which stands for a whole sentence, or by pressing a button next to a sentence displayed on the hand-held unit.

articleTitle: Reply by Mr. Sarkes Tarzian upon receiving the 1979 Consumer Electronics Award presented at the 1979 Chicago Fall Conference on Consumer Electronics
Phase Locked Loops and Surface Wave Filters an Ideal Combination
Trip Report on Consumer Electronics in China
Control IC for Switch Mode Power Supplies
abstract: Mains separatiQn in the entertainment field is used very widely because of its numerous advantages. One of the main reasons is the possibility of direct attachment to secondary sets e.g. earphones, video- recorders, cable converters, tapecorders, games and so on.

articleTitle: A Delay-Line-Less Video Signal Processing Circuit Using a New Surface Acoustic Wave Filter for Television Receivers
abstract: With the extensive use of highly integrated circuits, most of the circuitries for television receivers have been progressively rationalized. However, in contrast, the filter circuits for signal selection have not been improved enough.

articleTitle: Design for Reliability-Design for Litigation
abstract: Just as the oft-repeated TV commercial asks "How do you spell 'relief'?," and the answer is given as "R-O-L-A-I-D-S", an attorney would spell "consumer electronics" as "L-I-T-I-G-A-T-I-O-N." The very term" consumer electronics" identifies those products that will be produced in large numbers, used (and abused) by the masses, and which utilize electricity, that phenomenon well known for electrocuting people and starting fires.

articleTitle: Direct Broadcast Satellite (DBS)-A Historical View from Sputnik to now
A Video Surveillance System for Public Transaformation Vehicles Using 2-Way Land-Mobile Radio
abstract: A system has been developed to permit on-board vehicular surveillance by means of a closed-circuit TV, camera working with an FM two-way radio. This system has been installed on an AIRTRANS vehicle at the Dallas/ Ft. Worth airport in the fall of 1979. A snapshot is derived from the closed-circuit camera, to be transmitted in 3 seconds over a standard business or public safety channel. The pictures are composed of 16,384 picture elements (pixels), arranged as 128 lines, with 128 elements per line. The desirability of video surveillance is discussed, along with recent trends in electronics and communications that have helped to make it practical. An examination is then made into the general problem of sending visual information over narrowband FM radio, followed by a closer look at the specific bandwidth/resolution/time trade-offs that were made in the AIRTRANS system design.

articleTitle: 3.579545 MHz Can be More Than the Color Burst
abstract: There is a hardly a member of the entire American electronics profession that does not recognize 3.58 MHz as the NTSC* Color Burst standard. This frequency has been the standard for 25 years now, and practically all of us take it for granted that this peculiar frequency is strictly for television operation. As NMOS and the higher density HMOS silicon technology invade the province of Video Display Generation, the 3.58 MHz crystal will have to perform much more than its Color Burst function. In order to generate a video display to a "vanilla" (standard unmodified) television set, four frequencies are required: · VHF (or UHF) Channel Center Frequency The main channel frequency is channel 3 or 4 when generated by an IC Radio Frequency modulator, but may be any channel frequency from 2 through 82. · 3.579545 MHz Color Burst The televisions' color signals ride on the subcarrier that is 3.579545 MHz above the brightness modulated main carrier. Unlike the main channel frequency, the 3.579545 must be a very precise signal. · 6 MHz to 7.5 MHz Dot Clock The dot clock determines how many dots will be generated on a TV screen line. Of course, the more the better. The NTSC* allows only a 6 MHz bandwidth per channel, so the dot clock should be at least 6 MHz. If it does above 7.5 MHz though, the signal may be lost in the traps inside the television set.

articleTitle: An Automatic TV Signal Equalizer "Picture Clinic"
abstract: The paper describes an automatic Ghost canceller which has been developed and found suitable for consumer application.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluations of Selected Automatic Deghosting Systems for Television
abstract: The common problem of multipath reception manifests itself as "ghosts" in the resultant picture. Attempts to eliminate ghosts have included approaches involving special antennas, RF phase-delaying devices, or transversal equalizers that operate on the detected video waveform. This paper discusses experimental results that help to characterize the relative performance that can be obtained with transversal filters using various training waveforms and two popular adaptive control algorithms.

articleTitle: A New Chip and a New Package for Higher Power
abstract: The best of the state of the art in power handling with integrated circuits can be reached only if innova tions are introduced to both the chip and the package designs.

articleTitle: Microcomputers-Heritages and the Future
Developments in Plastic Optics for Projection Television Systems
abstract: In 1973, Advent Corp. introduced the first high-brightness, color projection-television system designed specifically for the consumer market. Although General Electric Co. was making excellent light-valve color systems, and Sony Corp. had produced single-tube systems, the Advent system, utilizing Schmidt-type reflective optics, is thought by many to be the most instrumental in stirring general public interest in projection television. This was followed by a less expensive unit Introduced in 1976 using aspheric plastic refractive optics. These earlier developments have led to the current intense activity to produce improved systems that will win consumer acceptance. It is no longer a question of when projection television will happen, but rather in what form, at what quality level, and at what price.

articleTitle: Integrated NTSC Chrominance/Luminance Processor
abstract: An intensive engineering effort in the past decade produced color TV receivers with a high degree of maturity. Although the price of receivers remained essentially unchanged, their performance and reliability were improved substantially. Among the many improvements in all sections of the receiver are not only those that relate to a better picture quality but also those responsible for reduced energy consumption, the simplified operation of controls, and reduced weight. In this paper attention will be focused on improvements in the chroma/ luma area.

articleTitle: Adaptation of U.K. Teletext System for 525/60 Operation
abstract: The United Kingdom (UK) Teletext System has now been in service in the UK f or four years. It is also being transmitted on a regular basis in more than six European countries and Australia. Experience has confirmed the soundness of the original system design concept which has lead to television sets equipped with decoders from a number of sources. These combine economy, ease of use, and rugged system performance. The small added cost for installing the teletext decoder has been one of the most important factors in establishing the service in Britain.

articleTitle: Development of VHF/FM Radio Front end Integrated Circuit
abstract: Recent years have witnessed an wide application of integrated circuits for radio receivers, with use including audio amplifiers, FM/AM IF amplifiers, FM/AM detectors, AM/RF amplifiers, mixers and FM stereo-demodulators. Moreover, a paper (1) describes a single chip AM/FM IC radio in which several of the above-mentioned functions have been integrated into a single chip.

articleTitle: Telesoftware-Value Added Teletext
abstract: The average person regards a radio receiver as a consumer device which he can buy at a relatively low cost from any multiple store, and which will supply him (at no extra cost) with entertainment, information and education. This radio is usually equipped with only a small number of controls (e.g. on/off, tuning, bandchange, volume) and it is very rare to find someone who is unable to operate it satisfactorily.

articleTitle: Enhanced UK Teletext Moves Towards Still Pictures
abstract: The UK teletext system has been a full public service for almost four years, and the specification of the system has remained unaltered. It is expected that by the end of 1980 there will be more than 100 000 teletext receivers in use. There is no doubt that the system rests on a firm technical foundation and the deliberate attempt made to stretch technology at the time the specification was formulated means that the system is giving the highest possible information transfer rate consistent with ruggedness and freedom from errors.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Terminal for the 1980's: Project Green Thumb
abstract: During this decade, low cost informatiom retrieval terminals (IRT's) will be available to consumers, professionals, and small businessmen. The mass marketing and distributiom of IRT's through retail outlets and the accompanying developement of an information service industry will make it possible for users to have access to vast information banks through existing communication facilities. Despite the obvious complexity of the regulatory enviornment in which the "information age is evolving, market acceptance, technological barriers, the energy crisis, a drive for increased productivity, and other socio-economic factors will encourage the development of information services and equipment. Teletext and videotext information services are already available in Great Britain, France, Germany, Canada and Japan. Many of these are in the test phase and are jointly sponsored by government and industry. In the U.S.A., the first federally funded test is a videotext style farm information retrieval system (FIRS), and is currently being tested in Kentucky. A description of this particular FIRS, Project Green Thumb, its implementation and its future significance is the subject of this dissertation.

articleTitle: 1980 Index IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics Vol. CE-26
abstract: This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the coauthors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.
